title: Product Packshot Photos for Multiple Views | AIVideosUGC
description: A packshot is a clean product photo on a plain background. Turn one photo of each side into front, back, top, and base views for your gallery or ads.
h1: Product Packshot Photos for Every Side You Photographed
lead: The speaker you already photographed, buttons and USB-C port included, can sit on a square with the backdrop you will reuse for the front. When the ad needs speech, those photos can carry a voice later.

steps.d: The set matches because the layout keeps one shared backdrop. Name the side first: front, buttons, or the face that shows the USB-C port.
A picture where the whole speaker is visible keeps the port you photographed. Buttons and the wrist strap stay where they are in that photo.
Save the square, then move to the speaker's next side. The next side is ready for a short ad with script, spoken voice, and captions.

faq.q: What does this side-view template include?
faq.a: It is a square setup for sides you already shot. Add the speaker photo that shows the buttons or the USB-C port, and download that view. Speech can be added later if the listing also needs a short ad.

faq.q: How do these templates get made?
faq.a: You get one square per side you upload. Start with the speaker's port side, keep the backdrop, and download that square before you do the front. A product link can supply words for a short ad, and your software can start the next side through the API.

faq.q: Why use this instead of filming a creator?
faq.a: The speaker photo you already have is enough for this listing. A second opening line for that ad can be cut without calling a crew back in.

Shops, listing managers, and agencies that need the speaker's front and port side, plus a spoken clip when the ad needs one. A person on screen is an AI avatar. Beginners can start from one clear photo.
Yes. Upload a clear photo of each side. You do not need a turntable. If you also make a video, set captions, a song, and an AI voice in the editor.

faq.q: Which products work with this template?
faq.a: The square layout fits the speaker and other goods with a front and a back, including the running shoe and the headphones in this set. Beauty, food, and fitness scenes sit in the same gallery when you want a video instead of a side photo.

faq.q: Can I use photos and clips I already shot?
faq.a: Yes. Bring a JPG, PNG, or WebP that shows the whole speaker, including the port and the wrist strap. A short clip you have the rights to can come in when the ad needs motion you already filmed.

faq.q: Which platforms are these files ready for?
faq.a: Each photo is square. A video from the same speaker photos can be 9:16, 1:1, 16:9, 4:3, or 3:4. A tall file fits a TikTok placement. A square fits a Facebook feed. YouTube can take the wide file, and Instagram can take the download. You can also post it yourself.

faq.q: Are these templates free to use?
faq.a: No. Each product photo spends 24 credits. A video is 24 credits for 6 seconds, 40 for 10, 60 for 15, or 120 for 30. You see the number first. If it fails, those credits come back. Starter is $24.50 a month for 200 credits, Pro is $35 for 300, and Premium is $63 for 600.

faq.q: Can I use these files in ads?
faq.a: Yes. Downloads have nothing stamped on them, so you can use them in listings, paid ads, and work you deliver for a client.

faq.q: Why use a template instead of starting from scratch?
faq.a: The square crop and the shared backdrop are already chosen. Your job is the speaker side you photographed, not building a frame from a blank file.

faq.q: Can one photo show a port that was hidden?
faq.a: No. Photograph that side and upload it. A made-up view is not a safe way to show a USB-C port, button, or wrist strap that was not in the photo.

steps.prompt: Front and back of the speaker on one plain background, with the port left as it was photographed.
